key_insight: Adding the ADR physical PV efficiency model to TSMixer did not consistently improve day-ahead solar power forecasting over a purely data-driven baseline.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, physics-informed model complexity may offer limited practical benefit beyond a modern neural forecasting architecture.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer through feature augmentation.
Build a second hybrid architecture using residual learning.
Compare convergence, accuracy, geographic transferability, and data efficiency.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries, showing slightly faster apparent convergence but no consistent gains in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
watch_item: The findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead PV forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed approaches.
paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
